title: Sprint, kanban and the board: the vocabulary of the week

videos.script: On your first Monday in a development team, somebody will say something like this. We are halfway through the sprint, the board is full, and your ticket is blocked, so pick something from the backlog. {{monday}} Every word in that sentence has a specific meaning, and nobody will stop to explain it. {{words}} This lesson is the vocabulary. Not because the words are hard. Each one is the name of an agreement about how the team works, and you are expected to keep the agreement from day one. {{agreement}} You will learn to read the board: what a column means, who moves a card, and why some columns have a limit on them. {{board}} You will learn what a sprint is, what happens at its start and at its end, and what the people called product owner and scrum master do. {{sprint}} And you will learn kanban, which gets rid of the sprint entirely, and what it uses instead. {{kanban}} Most teams you join will use some mixture of the two, with their own twist. By the end you will be able to recognise which parts they took from where, and ask the right questions in your first week. {{title}}
